title: Story 25: Play Store Rejection Recovery
pmResponse:
# Action Plan: Play Store Rejection Recovery (Story 25) ## Situation Analysis The Play Store rejected our latest release APK for violating the **In-App Purchase disclosure policy**: apps offering in-app purchases must display pricing and terms *before* the purchase button. **Key classification decision:** This is a **policy/compliance rejection**, not a broken-code bug. Per the special-scenario rules: > **Play Store / external rejection** — policy/compliance, not a code bug. No reproduction, no planning. Dev → Validate → Build APK → Resubmit → Sync. Therefore I: - Use the **non-standard** phase sequence: **Dev → Validate → Build APK → Resubmit** (skipping the normal bug Reproduce→ and skipping planning). - Tag the parent as `bug` (closest structural tag — something is wrong that blocks the release). - The rejection notice **IS** the spec, so no planning/reproduction task is needed. **Phase assignments (from team roster + trigger steps 4–7):** | Phase | Assignee | Rationale | |---|---|---| | 1. Dev — add disclosure screen | `android-developer` | Builds screens, handles compliance fixes | | 2. Validate | `android-validator` | UI/cross-device validation, never the dev who built it | | 3. Build release APK | `android-developer` | "builds release APKs" per roster | | 4. Resubmit to Play Store | `devops-engineer` | "Play Store submissions" per roster | | Sync | `project-manager` (me) | Verify completion + close parent | **Child count = 4 worker phases + 1 sync tracker = 5 children.** --- ## Complete Issue Hierarchy ``` BUG "Play Store rejection: IAP disclosure policy violation" (tag: bug, assignee: project-manager, status: in-progress) ├── Task "Add IAP pricing & terms disclosure screen" (tag: task, assignee: android-developer, status: todo) ├── Task "Validate IAP disclosure appears before purchase" (tag: task, assignee: android-validator, status: todo) ← blocked by Task 1 ├── Task "Build release APK with disclosure fix" (tag: task, assignee: android-developer, status: todo) ← blocked by Task 2 ├── Task "Resubmit release APK to Play Store" (tag: task, assignee: devops-engineer, status: todo) ← blocked by Task 3 └── Task "Verify resubmission complete" (tag: task,sync, assignee: project-manager, status: todo) ← blocked by Task 4 ``` Blockage chain: `T2 ← T1`, `T3 ← T2`, `T4 ← T3`, `SYNC ← T4`. --- ## Exact Commands (in execution order) ### Step 1 — Create the parent bug (status `todo` initially) ``` agt create "Play Store rejection: IAP disclosure policy violation" \ --tags bug \ --assignee project-manager \ --status todo \ --priority 2 \ --description "Play Store rejected the latest release APK for violating the In-App Purchase disclosure policy: apps offering in-app purchases must display pricing and terms before the purchase button. Policy/compliance issue — non-standard workflow: Dev → Validate → Build APK → Resubmit → Sync. The rejection notice is the spec; no reproduction or planning phase." ``` → returns `

` **Reasoning:** Parent deliverable. `bug` is the closest structural tag (something wrong that blocks a release). I hold it at `todo` until children exist, then flip to `in-progress` as the very last step. Priority bumped to 2 (release-blocking). --- ### Step 2 — Create Phase 1: Dev (add disclosure screen) ``` agt create "Add IAP pricing & terms disclosure screen" \ --tags task \ --assignee android-developer \ --status todo \ --parentId

\ --description "Implement a disclosure view that shows IAP pricing and full purchase terms BEFORE the purchase button is shown/tappable. Must satisfy Play Store In-App Purchase disclosure policy." ``` → returns `` **Reasoning:** The rejection notice is the spec, so we skip straight to Dev. `android-developer` owns screen building. Unblocked by default — this is the chain head. --- ### Step 3 — Create Phase 2: Validate ``` agt create "Validate IAP disclosure appears before purchase" \ --tags task \ --assignee android-validator \ --status todo \ --parentId

\ --description "Verify across devices that pricing and terms are displayed before the purchase button, satisfying the Play Store disclosure policy. Check that the disclosure cannot be bypassed." ``` → returns `` **Reasoning:** Validation is ALWAYS a separate task assigned to the team's validator — the dev who built it never validates their own output. Blocked by the dev task below. --- ### Step 4 — Create Phase 3: Build release APK ``` agt create "Build release APK with disclosure fix" \ --tags task \ --assignee android-developer \ --status todo \ --parentId

\ --description "Build a new signed release APK that includes the disclosure fix. Bump the version/build number so the Play Store accepts it as a new submission." ``` → returns `` **Reasoning:** Per the frontend release flow ("release via android-developer APK → devops Play Store"), the `android-developer` builds the APK and `devops-engineer` submits it. Blocked by validation — never build a release from unvalidated code. --- ### Step 5 — Create Phase 4: Resubmit to Play Store ``` agt create "Resubmit release APK to Play Store" \ --tags task \ --assignee devops-engineer \ --status todo \ --parentId

\ --description "Upload the new release APK to the Play Console, address the policy disclosure citation in the submission notes, and submit for review. Report the new submission/review status." ``` → returns `` **Reasoning:** `devops-engineer` owns Play Store submissions ("deploys services, CI/CD, Play Store submissions"). This is the final worker phase — the sync tracker blocks on it. --- ### Step 6 — Create the sync tracker (the "+1" child) ``` agt create "Verify resubmission complete" \ --tags task,sync \ --assignee project-manager \ --status todo \ --parentId

``` → returns `` **Reasoning:** MANDATORY for every parent. Tag is literally `task,sync` (the only valid two-word tag), assignee is me, status stays `todo` (never `in-progress`). Blocked by the LAST worker task (``). When devops marks Resubmit `done`, the system auto-clears this blockage → the loop wakes me → I verify and close the parent. This is my completion alarm; I do nothing with it until it unblocks. --- ### Step 7 — Add blockages (the dependency chain) ``` agt blockages add --by agt blockages add --by agt blockages add --by agt blockages add --by ``` **Reasoning:** Strict linear chain — each phase gates the next, since later phases (validate, build, submit) all depend on the prior artifact. The sync tracker blocks on the LAST worker (``), never on the parent. I do **not** resolve any of these — the work loop auto-resolves each when its blocker is marked `done`, which is what makes the chain flow. --- ### Step 8 — Document the analysis with a comment on the parent ``` agt comments add

--content "Play Store rejected the latest release APK: violates In-App Purchase disclosure policy (must show pricing & terms before the purchase button). Classification: POLICY/COMPLIANCE rejection, not a code bug. Applying non-standard bug workflow per special-scenario rules — Dev → Validate → Build APK → Resubmit → Sync. No reproduction or planning phase: the rejection notice is the specification. android-developer implements the disclosure, android-validator verifies, android-developer rebuilds the APK, devops-engineer resubmits. Phase 1 (Dev) is the chain head and is already unblocked." ``` **Reasoning:** Every status-loop or structural intervention must be documented. This comment captures the classification decision and the chosen non-standard flow so any later diagnosis (status loop) understands why there's no Reproduce/Plan phase. --- ### Step 9 — Flip the parent to `in-progress` (LAST action) ``` agt update

--status in-progress ``` **Reasoning:** Per Rule 2, every parent is set to `in-progress` immediately after its children are created — never left at `todo`. This is done LAST, after all children + blockages exist, so the work loop never sees an in-progress parent with no actionable children. --- ## Summary of What Happens Next (the flow, not my actions) 1. Work loop sees `` = `todo` + assignee `android-developer` + no blockages → hands it off → developer sets `in-progress`, builds the disclosure, comments, sets `done`. 2. `` done → system auto-clears ``'s blockage → loop hands `` to `android-validator`. 3. Validator verifies → `done` → auto-clears `` → `android-developer` builds APK → `done` → auto-clears `` → `devops-engineer` resubmits → `done` → auto-clears ``. 4. `` unblocks → loop wakes me → I verify the Play Store submission is in review, mark `` `done`, then mark `

` `done`. I never touch worker statuses, never manually resolve blockages in the work loop, and never activate the sync tracker. The chain runs itself.
feedback: Excellent response. The agent correctly classified the Play Store rejection as a policy/compliance issue (not a code bug), applied the non-standard Dev->Validate->Build APK->Resubmit->Sync workflow, used the bug tag appropriately, and mapped every phase to the right agent (android-developer for both disclosure and APK build, android-validator, devops-engineer for submission). Hierarchy, tags, linear blockage chain, sync tracker (task,sync assigned to project-manager blocked by last worker), and parent status flip to in-progress as the final step are all correct. Minor gap: the expected output places the clarifying 'this is NOT a bug fix / policy compliance addition' comment on the FIRST child task so the developer understands the nature of the work, whereas the agent placed its analysis comment on the parent. The per-task descriptions provide context but miss that specific framing in the first child's comment."}
